findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: CT logs list risky hostname staging.copperline.example with pattern staging, first_seen 2025-03-02, last_seen 2026-09-15; risky_hostnames_count=1, unique_hostnames=12.

findings.deal_impact: A publicly logged staging hostname may expose a less-hardened environment with weaker controls or test data; verify isolation, authentication, and data content before close as a value-protection item.

remediation.summary: Confirm staging host ownership and necessity; restrict to VPN/authenticated access, remove public exposure or retire it, and ensure no production data or credentials are present.

items.action: Confirm staging host ownership and necessity; restrict to VPN/authenticated access, remove public exposure or retire it, and ensure no production data or credentials are present.

deal_recommendations.text: Tie Proceed to a covenant requiring completion after close, within Days 61–100, of the staging-host restriction or retirement and confirmation that no production data or credentials are present, at $10K–$50K [F-001].
No adjustment to price is warranted under Proceed because total remediation of $10K–$50K is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band, with completion scheduled for Days 61–100 [F-001].

narrative.executive_summary:
Bottom line: Proceed with Copperline Analytics is recommended [F-001]. The rating is A on a score of 98.4 with no caps applied and low confidence, reflecting one medium-severity finding [F-001].

Key risks: A publicly logged staging hostname may expose a less-hardened environment with weaker controls or test data [F-001]. Public exposure leaves isolation and authentication unverified for that host [F-001]. Production data or credentials, if present, would extend exposure beyond a test system [F-001].

Management credibility: No contradiction pattern was identified, with 0 contradictions, 0 contradicted claims, 0 unsupported claims, and 0 supported claims, based on the single finding assessed [F-001].

Next steps: Confirm staging host ownership, isolation, authentication, and data content before close [F-001]. Require completion of the $10K–$50K remediation in Days 61–100 after close [F-001].
key_questions_for_management: Provide confirmation of ownership and business necessity for the staging hostname [F-001].
Confirm the isolation controls separating the staging environment from production [F-001].
Provide evidence of VPN or authenticated access restrictions for the staging host [F-001].
Confirm whether any production data is present in the staging environment [F-001].
Confirm whether any production credentials are present in the staging environment [F-001].
Provide the plan and timeline to remove public exposure or retire the staging host within Days 61–100 [F-001].

limitations: Unassessed CSF functions (no evidence from provided inputs): GV, DE, RC
Passive outside-in assessment only; no authenticated or internal testing
